notes: TWO FIXES, both found by a user reading the October column and not believing it. FIX 1 — UNPLANNED ONE-TIME SPENDING WAS BEING ABSORBED BY OTHER PLANS. The current-month rule 'count whichever is larger, spent or budgeted' was applied ONCE across the whole one-time group rather than per planned item, as it is for categories. An Rs 8,537 unplanned night out therefore vanished into the unspent headroom of an Rs 1,00,000 Diwali trip that had barely started, and the month looked no worse for it. The rule is now applied PER PLANNED ITEM, and unplanned spending ADDS on top because it has no budget to consume. This also realigns the projection sheet with the Budget page, which already rendered each plan as its own tube. FIX 2 — THE CURRENT MONTH COULD REPORT A LARGE NEGATIVE NET-TO-SAVINGS AND STILL CLOSE FLAT. Since v2026.05.05.15 the current month's closing savings was 'live balance minus card shortfall', which looks only at money that has already moved. With Rs 1.2L of planned spending still ahead, the sheet said Rs 66,594 had to come out of savings and then showed savings closing unchanged. Both could not be true. The current month now closes the way every future month already does: previous close + this month's net flow to savings. Verified: Rs 7,74,600 - Rs 61,594 = Rs 7,13,006, with the forward chain re-basing off it. WHY THIS IS SAFE NOW: the August failure that prompted the live-anchor was a close BELOW the live balance with no outflow to justify it, caused by the previous close being seeded from a PLANNED figure. Past months are now reverse-walked from actual logged transactions (_savingsAtEndOfMonth), so the previous close is trustworthy, and the drop here is justified by real expected outflow. Note the formula is algebraically identical to 'live balance + (target - what has already moved)'; the previous close is simply cheaper to compute. KNOWN CONSEQUENCE, STATED PLAINLY: if a salary-to-savings sweep larger than the month's net saving is made early in the month, the close will again sit below the live balance — because that money is expected to flow back out to cover the rest of the month's bills. That is the correct reading, but it is the same SHAPE as the August display that caused confusion before, so it is called out here deliberately. THE CARD TERM IS RETAINED and is not double-counting: an outstanding card balance is spending from EARLIER months, which this month's surplus does not contain. The salary account balance is deliberately NOT added back, because it mixes carried-over cash with this month's salary that surplus already counts; adding it wholesale would double-count the salary. Dashboard, Budget, Budget-actuals, Instruments, Rates and Decisions all re-run clean with no page errors. Engine, runProjection and the Decisions tab are untouched.
